title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 344 (Statement that company is in liquidation)

content.overview: Where a company is being wound up, whether by the Tribunal or voluntarily, every invoice, order for goods or business letter issued by or on behalf of the company or a Company Liquidator of the company, or a receiver or manager of the property of the company, being a document on or in which the name of the company appears, shall contain a statement that the company is being wound up. Contravention attracts fine of not less than fifty thousand rupees but which may extend to three lakh rupees on the company and every officer, the Company Liquidator and any receiver or manager who wilfully authorises or permits the non-compliance.
content.glance: Documents bearing the company name must state that the company is being wound up; wilful non-compliance attracts fine ₹50,000–₹3 lakh.
content.study: Section 344 is a disclosure obligation. Once a company is in winding up (Tribunal or voluntary), every invoice, order for goods or business letter issued by or on behalf of the company, the Company Liquidator, or a receiver or manager of its property, on which the company name appears, must contain a statement that the company is being wound up. The purpose is to put counterparties on notice of the liquidation. Contravention is punishable with fine of not less than fifty thousand and up to three lakh rupees on the company and every officer, the Company Liquidator and any receiver or manager who wilfully authorises or permits the non-compliance.

sections.heading: Disclosure duty
sections.body: Invoices, orders for goods and business letters bearing the company name must state that the company is being wound up.

sections.heading: Penalty
sections.body: Fine ₹50,000–₹3 lakh for company, officers, Liquidator, receiver/manager who wilfully authorise or permit non-compliance.

provisions.title: Statement that company is in liquidation

examples.title: Omitted statement
examples.body: A Company Liquidator issues invoices on company letterhead without stating that the company is being wound up. He is liable to fine under s. 344 if the omission was wilful.

hypotheticals.question: Does the duty apply only to Tribunal winding up?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 344 applies whether the company is being wound up by the Tribunal or voluntarily.
